subject: Activation MAP: staffing ramp, canary windows, and decision gates

Subject: Signed MAP + initial canary preferences

Hi Sean,

Thanks — attached is the signed Mutual Action Plan (signed-mpa.pdf). Procurement copied me on the final doc. We want to lock a short canary window in November, and then a wider rollout in mid-December. High level asks from our side:

- Confirm proposed canary windows (need 72h monitoring with rollback gates)
- Confirm training slots for product and ops (two half-day sessions)
- Share your staffing ramp (who will be on-call and handover dates)
- Confirm what logs/evidence you’ll provide during the canary for our security review

We’d like a single consolidated tracker (spreadsheet or Drive) with decision gates so our PM can sign off quickly. I’ve attached the signed MAP and put the procurement contact on copy.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Integrations
Heliomatrix

Elena — thanks for the signed MAP, and congrats on getting procurement across the line. Attaching our staffing ramp workbook (MPA-staffing-ramp.xlsx) and a first-pass canary calendar (summary below). I copied Marissa and Priyom to align training and runbooks.

Summary (first pass):
- Canary window: 2025-11-10 00:00 UTC -> 2025-11-13 00:00 UTC (72h monitoring).
- Rollout window: phased rollout starting 2025-12-14 over four weeks (regional phasing).
- Training: two half-day sessions (2025-11-03 and 2025-11-05) for product and ops; recorded session to be shared.
- Staffing: Tiered on-call schedule in workbook; primary SE handover on 2025-11-07.
- Evidence during canary: request/response latency, per-route error rates, KV cache hit ratio, sampling of audit logs (sample script provided).

Immediate asks for Heliomatrix:
1) Confirm the November canary window above or propose alternatives by EOD Friday.
2) Confirm two primary contacts for SSO & procurement (we need a technical contact for SSO smoke tests).
3) Approve the attached staffing ramp so we can publish the on-call calendar to both teams.

I’ll create a shared Drive tracker and post the acceptance criteria and rollback gates there; link will go to this thread once live.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Lead, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MPA-staffing-ramp.xlsx (Excel), canary-windows-calendar.ics (Calendar)

Adding the training and runbook details — scope below and a short acceptance checklist. I’ll own the training sessions and record them.

Training scope: product flows (end-to-end), invocations and throttling behaviors, incident playbook (fail-open vs fail-closed), and how to interpret per-route cost/latency dashboards.

Acceptance checklist for canary (we will run these daily during the 72h):
- Baseline traffic validation (synthetic load against pre-agreed scenarios)
- Latency 95th < 350ms for core routes
- Error rate < 0.5% sustained
- No data leakage incidents; audit log sampling passes (sample size 500 requests)
- SSO smoke test: successful login + token introspection in 5 minutes or less

Notes and considerations:
- If any daily gate fails, we escalate to a 2-hour triage with a decision to pause or rollback.
- We need your security contact to sign off on the audit sampling script (I’ve included a link in the Drive doc once I publish it).

I’ll follow up with the Drive link and training invites by end of day.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
